title: Ethiopian Fasting Calendar Food
localName: ጾም ቀን ምግብ — Tsom Qen Mgib
community: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — 200+ fasting days annually
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Fasting Calendar — the complete 200+ day fasting food tradition. The Ethiopian Orthodox calendar includes 55-day Lent, 40-day Advent, Apostles' Fast, Wednesday and Friday weekly fasts, and many others. The beyaynetu (ETH121), Shiro Firfir (ETH123), and all plant-based dishes are the food of this extraordinary commitment.
longDesc: The Ethiopian Orthodox fasting calendar produces the world's most extensive plant-based food tradition — 200+ days per year of vegan eating, producing a cuisine of extraordinary variety and depth.
ingredients: See ETH121 (Beyaynetu) as the complete weekly fasting meal
See ETH123 (Shiro Firfir) as the daily breakfast
See ETH101-ETH140 for the complete fasting repertoire
steps: Plan ahead — fasting periods require multiple dishes prepared.
Make large batches that improve over days.
Use the beyaynetu as the celebration fast meal.
Use shiro firfir as the practical daily meal.
chefTips: Ethiopian fasting food is not deprivation — it is an extraordinary culinary tradition.
commonMistakes: Thinking fasting food is limited — Ethiopia has over 40 distinct fasting dishes.
sustainabilityTips: The Ethiopian Orthodox fasting tradition is the world's most important institutional plant-based food tradition.
healthBenefits: 200+ days of plant-based eating provides extraordinary cardiovascular and metabolic health benefits.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian Orthodox fasting calendar is one of humanity's most remarkable dietary traditions — 200+ days per year of voluntary plant-based eating by an entire nation, producing a food culture that simultaneously is the world's most extensive vegan tradition and some of the world's most complex and varied vegetarian cooking.
